bullets.title: NVDA: Beat-and-raise consensus; FY28 guided to +75% but valuation/CEO transition dominate debate
bullets.body: NVDA reported ~$115.8B revenue with $107.6B data center sales and guided F4Q to $130B; FY28 growth raised to 75% from 70% despite halting ~$2.4B in Hopper/H200 China sales. Post-earnings debate centers on CEO transition risk (interim Colette Kress, permanent expected Q1 2027), 10Q filing delay for risk assessment additions, and CY28 visibility — UBS cut CY28 estimates ~15% while Piper lowered PT to $230 (from prior) on multiple compression to ~10x. DA Davidson prefers MU/AVGO over NVDA near-term; Vera Rubin ramp fastest in history at ~$20B first-quarter revenue; neocloud financing now subject to tighter credit scrutiny.

bullets.title: NVDA: MS TomorrowX — AMD, DELL, ALAB also bullish; infrastructure demand intact
bullets.body: MS TMT TomorrowX recap: AMD CEO says demand 'substantially higher' than supply with Venice/MI455 Helios performing 'extremely well' at META, MSFT, ORCL; DELL now has 6,500 AI factories; ALAB sees content per accelerator doubling every 18 months. CRM fell -9.5%, INTU -7.1%, NOW -6.5% amid unrelated internet disruptions. Agentic workloads account for ~80% of tokens; CPU revenue expected to 2x in FY28.

bullets.title: TTWO: GTA VI scores 99 Metacritic (all-time record), tracking $1.8B+ in first 3 days
bullets.body: GTA VI received a 99 Metacritic score tying the all-time record (Zelda Ocarina of Time); Sensor Tower estimates 17M+ units/$1.65B revenue already; UBS estimates 37M units/$3.3B gross sales for the December quarter. DA Davidson notes pre-orders at 10.31M as of 11/9, up 36.6% in 8 days. TTWO trading ~15% below 52-week high ahead of launch; GTA V comparison is 16M units in first 3 days.

bullets.title: DIS: Q4 beats across segments; analysts raise targets on parks strength and double-digit FY27 EPS guide
bullets.body: Disney Q4 EPS $1.77 beat consensus $1.67; revenue $25.95B beat $25.16B; FY27 EPS guided to double-digit growth vs Street at +8.5%. Domestic parks attendance up 11%, SVOD OI beat +17.8%. Needham raises PT to $135, Wells Fargo to $140, Goldman to $143 (all Buy/Overweight). NTM P/E of 15.2x vs 5-yr avg 19.0x; 84% of sell-side at Buy.

bullets.title: MDB: Downgraded to short at Hedgeye; CEO/exec exodus stalls large enterprise deals
bullets.body: Hedgeye moved MDB to Short Bench on Nov 15 following CEO CJ Desai's departure for Meta; Chief Customer Officer Erica Volini, AI head Pablo Stern-Pablo Stern-Plaza, and 7+ sales reps have also left. FY27 revenue estimate cut to $3,009M from $3,100M; FY28 cut to $3,668M from $3,849M. GS notes MDB approaching 30x non-GAAP P/E on FY28 and investor conviction at multi-month lows.

bullets.title: DDOG: AI-driven modernization accelerating; core ex-large-customer growing low-to-mid 30%+
bullets.body: At RBC TIMT Conference, Datadog management said the core business ex-large customer is growing low-mid 30% or better, with infrastructure monitoring still mid-30s. Bits AI is the fastest-adopted product ever, used by ~one-third of customers; monetization still small. The large-customer headwind is framed as a one-quarter normalization after early renewal/minimum commitment guidance.

bullets.title: NET: Cloudflare — GAAP profitability path pulled forward ~2 years; AI agents major growth vector
bullets.body: Cloudflare conference commentary: AI agent workloads are a major new demand source; network now covers ~30% of web. Revenue upside is stronger than expected with leading indicators (pipeline, RPO, retention) all strong. Path to GAAP profitability moved forward by almost 2 years as Workers/Workers AI unit economics improve at scale.

bullets.title: MSFT: Azure-ByteDance $500M cloud deal disclosed; Ignite reinforces AI monetization beyond Copilot
bullets.body: Microsoft is in advanced talks to provide $500M of cloud computing to ByteDance (primarily OpenAI models on Azure); ByteDance on track to spend $1B+/year on MSFT AI/cloud services; deal has upset OpenAI. Separately, Citi's Tyler Radke reiterates Buy as MSFT top mega-cap pick, noting Ignite reinforces M365/Copilot demand, E7 adoption, and Fabric/agent deployment.

bullets.title: CRM: Post-CFO departure pullback viewed as overblown; 2H ARR guidance conservative
bullets.body: DA Davidson says the CRM CFO departure was compensation-driven ($60M IonQ offer vs $6-7M at CRM) and not a business signal. Expects 2H ARR to stabilize at ~20% Y/Y with potential reacceleration to ~21% by FQ4. CRM fell -9.5% amid internet disruption on 11/18 per MS TMT note.

bullets.title: ARM: MS raises conviction in ~$2B AGI CPU opportunity FY27-28; supply approaching demand
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reiterates Equal-weight on ARM but says confidence is growing in the ~$2B AGI CPU sales opportunity across FY27-28, with supply commitments approaching that level and demand well above it. Data centers are the brighter royalty spot vs. handsets; v10 architecture to focus on AI compute and security; triple-digit data center revenue growth expected in outer years.

bullets.title: RIOT: MS raises PT to $41 from $35.50 on 900MW Corsicana lease generating ~$11B shareholder value
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised RIOT's price target to $41 from $35.50, citing the 900MW Corsicana powered-shell lease at 33% return on cost generating potential $11.1B in net shareholder value (~2x current market cap). GenAI power bottlenecks of 70GW through 2028 underpin the thesis; recent PSP stock weakness (RIOT, HUT, CIFR) viewed as a buying opportunity.

bullets.title: EQIX/DLR: Citi upgrades both on AI/hyperscale demand; recurring revenue growth to accelerate to 13% in 2027
bullets.body: Citi upgraded EQIX (top pick) expecting recurring revenue growth to accelerate to 13% in 2027; maintains Buy on DLR with positive demand commentary and double-digit core FFOPS growth expected. BXDC acquires Amazon data centers for $5B at 7% cash cap rate. US data center construction starts declined in Q3 for first time in over a year; Loudoun County approved 12-month pause on new DC applications.

bullets.title: NYT: Citi downgrades to Neutral, cuts PT to $76 from $85 on six eroding engagement metrics
bullets.body: Citi downgraded NYT from Buy to Neutral and cut the PT from $85 to $76, citing deterioration across six key indicators: app downloads, active users, engagement frequency/time, organic web visits, and monetization deceleration. AI overviews are reducing organic search traffic to nytimes.com. NYT fell -3.8% in pre-market on the news.

bullets.title: NFLX: Co-CEO Sarandos bullish on international, live sports, AI efficiency; YouTube competition acknowledged
bullets.body: Netflix co-CEO Sarandos highlighted 16% revenue growth, strong live sports performance, and ~80% of members watching Korean content. AI is improving production and content discovery. YouTube is an increasingly relevant competitor via podcasts and creator programming. Interactive entertainment and sports betting represent next growth frontiers.

bullets.title: MRVL/CRDO: Patent dispute settled; both appear at CES 2027 investor meetings
bullets.body: Marvell and Credo settled their patent dispute over data-center cable technology. Both stocks appear on Jefferies and Goldman CES 2027 investor meeting rosters (Jan 5-7, Las Vegas) alongside MU and SNDK.

bullets.title: SPOT: Jefferies hosting investor HQ visit Dec 1 in NYC; limited to 5 investors
bullets.body: Jefferies arranged a Spotify HQ investor visit on December 1 at 4 World Trade Center in NYC, limited to 5 investors. Head of IR Bryan Goldberg participates. Spotify has 300M+ paying subscribers and 770M+ MAUs.

bullets.title: NVDA/HUT/WULF: Powered-shell thesis reinforced by NVDA's 'land, power, shell' financing priority and Texas TCEQ permit
bullets.body: NVDA interim CEO Colette Kress stated land, power, and shell availability is a critical priority for future data-center financing support. Texas TCEQ approved an air permit for 35 turbines (up to 750 MW) in Brownsville, TX; ERCOT comprehensive review deadline is December 10. HUT and WULF cited as beneficiaries of the powered-shell tailwind.

bullets.title: UBS equity finance: Tech net short, AI/semis covering; better short in neocloud/leveraged infra
bullets.body: UBS equity finance shows US Technology net short with shorts +10.9% WoW. Top short interest increases include COHR +41.6%. Top covers: GOOG, AMZN, META, LITE, MU. UBS view: AI/semis easy short largely exhausted as HFs cover and real money buys dips; better short setup in leveraged neocloud/infrastructure vs self-funded hyperscalers.

bullets.title: PANW: Upbeat pre-earnings tone; NGS ARR +63% y/y, RPO +34-35%; thematically 'right way' AI name
bullets.body: GS TMT notes positive market sentiment around PANW ahead of earnings as a thematically correct AI security name. F1Q guidance shows stable NGS ARR growth of +63% y/y and RPO +34-35% y/y.

bullets.title: INTU: Mizuho hosting FQ1 earnings debrief call 11/19; stock down -7.1% amid internet outage
bullets.body: INTU fell -7.1% on 11/18 amid widespread internet disruptions per MS TMT. Mizuho analyst Siti Panigrahi hosting an INTU FQ1 earnings debrief call on November 19 at 8pm ET.
